story: US-19 (S4-7): the rank order under random 10% weight changes
counted: briefs with 2 or more shown products; one with fewer has no order to change

what_counts.median: Today's number compares the places of every shown product, each in its own position.
what_counts.untied: The second number gives each group of products the app marks "too close to call" one shared place, the average of its members' places, so a reorder inside a group moves nothing and any other move counts.

note: No change reordered any of the five briefs' shown products: in them they are far apart, so this shows the order holds there, not how close products behave. The close brief beside them (`close`, D-74) is the check that can fail: there, changes do reorder the shown products.

close.note: The median Spearman, 0.8929, is below US-19's target of 0.9: on close products a 10% change of the weights reorders the shown products often enough to miss it. Reported as it is, never tuned to pass.

measures.source: backend/tests/fixtures/decide/stability/close_earbuds.json (made up), 100 weight changes of up to 10%, seed 19, app.decide
measures.detail: The close brief's median Spearman between its shown order and each changed one.
